correctness.rationale: Column sections of a strong-product independent set have cardinalities zero, one, or two. Each nonadjacent two-set in C5 has union of closed neighborhoods all five symbols and forces both adjacent columns empty. If D and E are doubled and empty columns then D±1⊆E; hence |I|=n+|D|−|E|≤n. Cyclic ±2 singleton constructions achieve n for every n≥6 (for odd n use a five-cycle plus two-step backtracks). Equality implies |D|=|E| and D+1=D−1=E, i.e. D+2=D. If D empty all columns are singleton and their symbols trace a closed ±2 walk; if D nonempty then n is even and D is exactly one parity class, the other empty. Each occupied double section has five freely chosen C5 nonadjacent pairs. The all-length labeled count follows by choosing a0 (5), k positive signs satisfying 2k≡n(mod5), plus 2·5^(n/2) even-n codes. Independently reconstructed cyclic column-state transfer enumeration from the actual graph and got alpha n and counts 350,70,1600,360 for n=6,7,8,9; finite tests support but do not replace the equality proof. C5 spectrum gives the even/odd asymptotic growth as submitted.

value.rationale: Counting every optimal codebook in a canonical zero-error confusability product is a substantive complete classification for a natural infinite graph family. The two structurally different extremizer mechanisms and parity split n-even ~5^(n/2) versus n-odd ~2^n supply mathematically meaningful design diversity, without asserting new Shannon capacity or arbitrary-product results.

final_claim: For n≥6, all labeled maximum independent sets of C5⊠Cn have size n and are exactly (i) cyclic one-word-per-column ±2 walks or (ii) for even n alternating empty/two-word columns, giving 5∑_(2k≡n mod5)binom(n,k)+[2|n]2·5^(n/2) optimal sets.
